angles.angle: Consumer culture has made possessions more disposable, weakening their sentimental value
angles.example: fast fashion items are often discarded within a season, unlike a grandparent's hand-repaired tools

angles.angle: Frequent upgrading of devices and clothing has a significant environmental cost
angles.example: the demand for the latest smartphone model contributes to e-waste and rare-earth mining

angles.angle: Right-to-repair regulation is one practical way to extend product lifespans
angles.example: some countries now require manufacturers to provide spare parts for years after a product launches

angles.angle: Possessions can serve as anchors for memory and identity, not just utility
angles.example: a worn-out journal can hold more personal meaning than its replacement value suggests
expressions: a tangible link to the past

angles.angle: Minimalism as a counter-trend suggests changing attitudes toward materialism
angles.example: younger generations increasingly favour experiences over owning physical goods
